name: Exness
description: Exness is a Cyprus-headquartered forex and CFD broker founded in 2008, self-described as the world's largest retail broker by trading volume. Regulated by the FCA, CySEC, FSA Seychelles, CBCS Curacao, FSC BVI, and FSC Mauritius, it offers 200+ instruments across MetaTrader 4, MetaTrader 5, Exness Terminal, and the Exness Trade mobile app. The majority of global retail clients are routed to the FSA Seychelles entity.

sections.heading: Is Exness Worth Your Money in 2026?
sections.body:
Sixteen years in operation, trading volumes that dwarf most competitors, and a withdrawal system that genuinely processes 95% of requests in under a minute — independently confirmed across multiple community sources. That last point alone sets Exness apart from the field. The Raw Spread account charges $7 round-turn on near-zero EUR/USD spreads, putting it on par with IC Markets and Pepperstone for cost-conscious scalpers. And the $1 minimum deposit on Standard means there is almost no barrier to testing the waters.

The catch is structural, not operational. Your account almost certainly sits under FSA Seychelles — an offshore regulator with no investor compensation scheme and limited enforcement capacity. The FCA and CySEC licences exist, but they serve UK and EU residents only. If you deposit from India, Nigeria, or Thailand, those Tier-1 badges on the homepage are decorative for your purposes. Unlimited leverage sounds like a feature until you realise it is only available on the entity with the weakest client protections.

Exness suits experienced traders who want speed and low costs — and who accept the trade-off of offshore regulation knowingly.

sections.heading: Is Exness Regulated? — Licence Check 2026
sections.body:
Yes — Exness holds licences from two Tier-1 regulators (FCA and CySEC) plus several offshore and mid-tier authorities. But the critical question is not whether Exness is regulated. It is which entity regulates YOUR account.

Exness (UK) Ltd operates under FCA licence 730729. UK residents get FSCS coverage up to GBP 85,000 and leverage capped at 1:30 on major pairs. Exness (Cy) Ltd holds CySEC licence 178/12, offering EU/EEA clients ICF protection up to EUR 20,000 with the same 1:30 cap. These are legitimate, meaningful protections.

For the vast majority of Exness's global client base — traders in India, Indonesia, Vietnam, Thailand, Philippines, UAE, Saudi Arabia, Egypt, South Africa, Nigeria, Pakistan, and Brazil — the operating entity is Exness (SC) Ltd, regulated by FSA Seychelles under licence SD025. No compensation scheme exists. No external ombudsman. Leverage runs up to unlimited for accounts under $5,000 equity. Funds are held in segregated accounts (broker-stated) but segregation without a compensation scheme means you are an unsecured creditor if the entity becomes insolvent.

The FSCA South Africa licence adds a mid-tier layer but provides no compensation fund either. The CBCS Curacao and FSC BVI licences are administrative — they do not add meaningful retail protection. NAFT last reviewed Exness regulation in January 2026.

sections.body:
Accepted: India, Indonesia, Vietnam, Thailand, Philippines, UAE, Saudi Arabia, Egypt, South Africa, Nigeria, Pakistan, Brazil, United Kingdom, EU/EEA member states, most of Sub-Saharan Africa, most of the MENA region, most of South and Southeast Asia, and parts of Latin America.

Not accepted: United States, Canada, Australia, New Zealand, Singapore, Malaysia, Israel, Myanmar, Vatican City, US territories (Guam, Puerto Rico, US Virgin Islands), North Korea, Iran, Syria, Crimea, Cuba.

Entity routing matters more than simple acceptance. A trader in the UK opens under the FCA entity with FSCS compensation and 1:30 leverage. A trader in Germany routes to CySEC with ICF coverage. But a trader in India, Nigeria, or the UAE — despite being accepted — routes to FSA Seychelles with unlimited leverage and zero investor protection. Same broker, completely different risk profile depending on your passport.
sections.practical_note: If you are outside the UK and EU, confirm your assigned entity in your Exness personal area immediately after registration. Your regulatory protections — or lack thereof — depend entirely on which entity you land under.

sections.heading: Exness Spreads, Fees and Accounts — What Do You Actually Pay in 2026?
sections.body:
Five account types, ranging from a $1-deposit beginner account to a zero-spread professional setup. The maths differs significantly between them.

Standard is the entry point — no commission, spreads publicly reported at 0.6-1.5 pips on EUR/USD across independent sources. That translates to $6-$15 all-in per standard lot. Acceptable for swing traders, expensive for scalpers. Standard Cent mirrors this but in cent lots — useful for testing strategies with real money at negligible risk.

Pro offers instant execution with tighter spreads (broker-stated from 0.3 pips) and no commission. The catch: instant execution means requotes during volatility. If you trade NFP or FOMC, expect slippage or rejections on this account type.

Raw Spread is where serious scalpers land. Near-zero EUR/USD spread plus $7 round-turn commission — genuinely competitive with IC Markets and Pepperstone Razor. All-in cost: roughly $7-$8 per lot on EUR/USD during London/New York sessions.

Zero advertises 0.0 pips on 30 instruments with commission varying from $0.20 to $3.50 per side depending on the pair. On EUR/USD specifically, the Zero account can be cheaper than Raw Spread — but on exotic pairs, the commission inflates substantially. Read the full commission schedule before assuming this is the cheapest option across all instruments.

Leverage is the elephant in the room. Under FCA and CySEC, you get 1:30 on majors — standard retail cap. Under FSA Seychelles, accounts below $5,000 equity can access unlimited leverage. This is marketed as a feature. It is a liquidation accelerator for anyone who does not understand position sizing intimately.

sections.heading: How Fast Can You Get Your Money Out of Exness?
sections.body:
Speed is where Exness genuinely separates from the pack. The broker claims 95% of withdrawals process in under 60 seconds — and this is independently confirmed across community forums, app store reviews, and trader groups in Asia and Africa. Instant is not a marketing word here; it is the operational reality for most standard withdrawal requests.

Visa, Mastercard, Skrill, Neteller, Perfect Money, and USDT (Tether) all process instantly for most users (broker-stated, independently confirmed). Bank wire is the exception — up to 3 business days depending on your bank and jurisdiction. No withdrawal fees on any method (broker-stated). The $1 minimum applies across most electronic methods.

The one scenario where speed reportedly breaks down: very large withdrawals (five figures and above) may trigger additional compliance review. This is standard across the industry but worth noting given the single large-sum complaint that surfaced publicly in early 2026.

table.footnote: Processing times are broker-stated and independently confirmed across multiple community sources for standard withdrawal amounts. Large withdrawals may require additional compliance checks.

sections.heading: Exness Withdrawals in 2026 — The Real Picture
sections.body:
Community feedback is overwhelmingly positive on withdrawal speed. Across trader groups in India, Indonesia, Nigeria, and the UAE, the consistent report is that e-wallet and crypto withdrawals arrive in under a minute. This is not the norm for the industry — most brokers take 24-48 hours minimum — and it represents a genuine operational advantage that builds trust.

The negative pattern is narrow but notable. One publicly reported complaint from January 2026 claims $347,165 in USDT was seized by Exness citing technical manipulation and fake candles. This remains unverified and represents a single data point from an enormous client base. But for a complaint of that size to surface publicly at all warrants mention. Separately, a small number of community reports mention extended verification requests on first-time large withdrawals — again, standard industry practice but occasionally frustrating for traders who funded via crypto expecting anonymity.

If a withdrawal stalls: first, check your Exness personal area for any pending verification requests. Second, contact support via live chat — response times are generally fast. Third, if unresolved after 48 hours, escalate via email with your account number and transaction ID. Document everything. There is no external ombudsman for Seychelles entity clients — your escalation path is internal only, which is precisely why the instant processing on normal amounts matters so much for building confidence before scaling up.

sections.body: No broker operating at this scale is without concerns, and Exness has several that deserve direct acknowledgement. The regulatory structure is the primary issue — not because Exness is unregulated, but because the regulation that covers most of its clients offers minimal protection. The unlimited leverage marketing compounds this by attracting precisely the traders least equipped to handle it. NAFT last reviewed Exness in January 2026.

Self-described as world's largest retail broker — extraordinary claim, difficult to independently verify, and scale does not equate to safety.

sections.heading: Who Should Use Exness — and Who Should Not
sections.body: The answer depends entirely on your experience level and what you prioritise. Exness is not a bad broker — but it is a broker where knowing what you are getting into matters more than usual.
not_for: Beginners who do not yet understand leverage and position sizing — unlimited leverage will destroy an underfunded account faster than any education section can prevent.
Traders who require Tier-1 compensation scheme protection on their deposits — if you are outside the UK or EU, you have none here.
Anyone treating the unlimited leverage as a shortcut to scaling — it is not a feature, it is a risk multiplier that favours the house.
Traders who want an external ombudsman or dispute resolution body — Seychelles entity clients have no independent escalation path.
for: Experienced scalpers and day traders in India, Indonesia, Vietnam, Thailand, UAE, or Nigeria who prioritise execution speed and instant withdrawals above all else.
High-frequency traders who need the Raw Spread account's $7 round-turn at near-zero EUR/USD spreads — genuinely competitive.
Traders comfortable with offshore regulation who want the lowest possible minimum deposit ($1) to test a broker before committing larger capital.
USDT-native traders who fund and withdraw in Tether and want instant crypto processing without conversion fees.
Swing traders using Standard or Pro accounts who value the zero-commission structure and accept the wider spreads as a trade-off.

sections.heading: How to Open an Exness Account — Step by Step
sections.body: Registration is fast — Exness has streamlined the process to get traders funded within minutes rather than days.

steps.title: Register
steps.detail: Visit exness.com and click the registration button. You need an email address and phone number. Choose your account type — Standard if you are testing with small capital, Raw Spread or Pro if you already know your trading style. The process takes under two minutes.

steps.title: Verify your identity (KYC)
steps.detail: Upload government-issued ID (passport or national ID card) and proof of address (utility bill or bank statement dated within 3 months). Exness states verification typically completes within hours, though some regions may take longer. Full withdrawal access requires completed KYC.

steps.title: Fund your account and test a withdrawal
steps.detail: Deposit via your preferred method — $1 minimum on Standard accounts. Immediately place one small trade, then request a withdrawal of any amount. If it processes instantly as expected, you have confirmed the withdrawal pipeline works for your method and jurisdiction. Scale from there with confidence.

sections.practical_note: Make a small deposit. Place one trade. Request a withdrawal immediately. If it processes cleanly, scale with confidence. This is the single best test of any broker — and with Exness's instant processing, you will know within a minute whether your withdrawal path works.

sections.heading: Exness Final Verdict — Is It Worth It in 2026?
sections.body:
NAFT rates Exness 7.5 out of 10 with a star rating of 3.7/5. The withdrawal speed is genuinely exceptional — few brokers in this industry deliver instant processing at this scale, and it is independently confirmed rather than marketing fiction. Raw Spread costs are competitive with IC Markets and Pepperstone. The $1 minimum deposit removes barriers to entry. On pure operational metrics, Exness performs well.

The risks are structural. Most of the global client base sits under FSA Seychelles with no compensation scheme, no external ombudsman, and leverage that can liquidate an account in seconds. The FCA and CySEC licences are real but irrelevant for traders outside the UK and EU — and that covers the vast majority of Exness's users. One large unverified complaint from early 2026 does not make a pattern, but the lack of external recourse for offshore clients means any dispute becomes your word against theirs.

If you are an experienced trader who understands position sizing, wants fast withdrawals, and accepts offshore entity risk knowingly, Exness is a legitimate option that delivers on its core promises. NAFT recommends starting with a small deposit, verifying the withdrawal pipeline personally, and scaling only once you are satisfied. If regulatory protection matters to you more than speed, compare IC Markets or Pepperstone under their ASIC and CySEC entities where your funds carry actual compensation scheme backing.
